criteria.rationale: The previous seven reviews and first native attestation retain their stated evidence boundaries. POSIX user/root trust is explicit; Windows ACL privacy is excluded, native Windows and live/recursive vendor execution were not established, and the independently adapted broad suite was not green. Current 159/159 native validation is supplied evidence at the sealed HEAD. F1-F5 preserve owners and review dates, including unproven late-copy scheduling and stronger reservation authentication. Declaring the existing capability adds no new privacy or independence guarantee.

Whole-prompt transfer, refusal handback, reservation and pinned-root lifecycle regressions pass in the module lane. Round-7 focused detach/state race run passed in the disclosed ownership-adapted external copy. R3-03 is bounded by conservative grace waiting; deterministic copy-result scheduling remains open as F2, not claimed tested by an unrelated registered race selection.

CLI task/resume, parser and MCP refusal are covered by delegation integration. R1-03 refusal status is fixed; R4-01 canonical observer identity, R5-01 six legacy continuation cases and R6-01 foreign-history CLI/MCP parity were resolved in subsequent reviews and confirmed in round 7.

Typed foreground-equivalent refusals, lone-dash parsing, reset-wait refusal, unsafe path rejection and missing-cwd refusal are covered. R4-02 fallback no longer launches through an unchecked alias. Pre-existing history-check early-error JSON is open as F4 and is not certified as a passing diagnostic contract.

Shared engine, built CLI and MCP refusal/continuation paths were reviewed across rounds 1-7. Round 7 independently reran MCP/parser probes and negative foreign-history preview/apply cases. Current registered delegation integration passes; assessment consumer gaps remain disclosed.

Task attempt, log, marker and record-place handback, history loss and refusal context remain actionable. Inherited observation and MCP presentation/cancellation limits remain owned in knowledge:delegation-observation-round4 and knowledge:delegation-mcp-round5. F4 retains the unrelated history-check error-document defect.

Round 7 approved R1-R11 after R4-01 canonical history, R4-02 missing-cwd, R5-01 legacy resume/handoff and R6-01 inherited foreign-root fixes. Six same-project legacy cases pass. Relative XDG and unsafe POSIX ancestor/component locations are intentionally refused and documented as breaking; legacy spelling is read only when associated with the selected resolved root. No migration or native Windows behavior is claimed.

Round-7 focused production paths and independent probes passed; baseline-first M24, M31 and combined M30+M31 fail intended assertions. Earlier rounds cover pipe, ownership and refusal regressions. Independent broad full suite was not green under the disclosed host ownership/Git-fixture constraints; not all broad failures were root-caused. Current sealed strict module evidence is supplied separately and passes.

The delegation ADR and parent spec require first-class background tasks and identify detach/state F2/F3. Reusing the existing bounded supervisor addresses missing detach without a daemon; anonymous prompt pipes avoid replaceable/leaking spool files, private resolved path chains and a pinned root prevent directory redirection, and sanitized controls plus same-root legacy-history binding address the reproduced foreign-history cause. Round-7 M24/M31 and combined M30+M31 discriminate these mechanisms; integration validates the production CLI/MCP composition. The bundle structural observation is present and binds the unchanged implementation digest; it is not a separate behavioral proof.

Four manuals, help, MCP guidance, changelog and spec were inspected over seven rounds. R1-05 MCP wording and R1-06/R2-02 obsolete spool text were corrected; R3-02/R4-04 platform/refusal and breaking-change disclosures were reconciled. Current Final Report preserves Windows ACL/build-only limits, handback trust and inherited handoffs, plus owned F1-F5. Its broad mutation summary is implementer-supplied, not an independent replay of every mutant. No documentation build is inferred from this Go build ref.

Detached task and piped resume handback, watch/wait/list and foreground refusal parity satisfy the reviewed contract. Checkout ancestor refusal requires repairing/moving the checkout, not merely changing XDG. F1 tracks Windows casing/native ACL evidence; F2 copy scheduling; F3 stronger reservation authentication; F4 pre-existing history-check JSON; F5 task-derived usage-limit routing. All remain open with owners and 2026-11-26 review dates. F5 is maintainer-recorded follow-up context, not a newly independently reproduced defect.

The current requirement trace maps R1-R11 to named delegation integration and unit tests. Round 7 judged each satisfied within its documented platform model, including whole prompt, exit parity, owner seams, pinned root, canonical history and same-project legacy continuation. Current HEAD validation is bound to the sealed subject; Windows privacy and recursive/live vendor execution are not implied.

Compared 6b6f2777..5963dee7: no source changes; only delivers frontmatter and Delivery targets section, retained three bundles and prior attestation, plus refreshed indexes/results. Implementation digests match both seals. Declaring capability:delegation-task with module:pose-mcp profile:composed-capability entrypoint:pose-mcp/internal/cli/delegate_task.go is correct: the parent spec declares that same capability/entrypoint and explicitly spawned detach/state follow-ups F2/F3. This extends its existing task execution and private history, not a separately consumed capability. Current surface-check verifies composition and fresh integration evidence. Prior blockers remain resolved and F1-F5 remain explicit; approval does not close the spec or retire launchers.

R1-01/02 replace the replaceable/leaking spool with a pipe; R1-04 adds owner regressions; R2-01 requires completed copy and reservation; R3-01 pins validated paths; R4-02 refuses lost cwd; R6-01 sanitizes inherited controls and independently binds legacy history to the selected root. Round 7 found no blocker in the POSIX trust model. User/root mutation of their own private tree remains excluded; F3 tracks stronger existing-attempt authentication. F1 retains a medium Windows ACL/platform limitation outside the privacy guarantee, not downgraded or waived by approval; casing alone is low R7-01. No native Windows, multi-UID, live vendor or recursive detach evidence is claimed. Credential-pattern diff review found no material; dedicated scanners were unavailable and no dependency changed.

The smallest sufficient solution extends the existing task capability and supervisor with prompt transfer, private-path validation and root/history binding. A new daemon, queue, scheduler, migration or MCP task-start authority would exceed the explicit non-goals. Leaf chmod alone leaves replaceable ancestors; sanitation alone lacks independent same-root binding; a file spool retains exposure/replacement risk. Existing read-only legacy lookup bounds compatibility cost. Reconsider if native Windows ACL privacy or hostile user/root mutation enters scope, or F2/F3 evidence disproves current conservative copy/handback assumptions; those need stronger mechanisms, not a renamed capability.
